label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Draft post:**

Good news first, then an apology, and then a change to how we charge.

Priya Bhatia, chartered (IStructE), joins us on Monday 16 November. She has spent nine years at a consultancy in Coventry and she is very good at what she does. She has also just solved a problem I created for myself.

I need to be honest with you about the last two months. Turnaround on beam calculations and drawings ran at five to six weeks through September and October, and a few of you waited far too long. One of you left a sharp review, which was fair, and I am sorry. If you were waiting on drawings, your job is moving now and you can message me directly.

Why it happened, in plain terms: I was doing site visits in the day and calculations until midnight. My wife started calling the office "the other house." The slow weeks were my fault — I said yes to too much work on my own and did not have the nerve to turn any of it down. Things have already been quicker since October, and with Priya here our target is 10 working days for beam calculations and drawings, from instruction to issue.

One example. A couple in Harborne had their builder standing waiting with the steel already ordered. We got the calculations to them in three days, but only after they chased me twice. That should not have been necessary.

The other change: from 1 January 2027 our first site visit will cost £95, credited in full against the fee if you go ahead with the work. Any visit already booked when this post goes up stays free, whatever date it falls on.

I would rather explain the reasoning than hide it. The free visit was generous, but around a third of visits never turned into a job, and that time is the same time your drawings are waiting. Charging from January means fewer wasted slots and shorter waits for everyone actually instructing.

If you are one of the people who has been waiting, message me. If you see Priya on site, do say hello — she is joining us and she deserves a proper welcome.

Right. Better, quicker, and more honest. that is the plan.

---

Around 385 words. Two judgement calls worth flagging: I kept the Harborne story because it shows you fixed it, but cut the "my fault" repetition to avoid sounding like you're dwelling; and I framed the £95 as starting 1 January 2027 with the free-visit guarantee pinned to "booked when this post goes up" so nobody has to guess. If you'd rather not name the review publicly, say so and I'll rework that line to "a few of you were unhappy and one of you has told us so" without pointing at it.
